info.title: rnfs local API
info.summary: The JSON API of a running rnfs daemon, on the loopback only.
info.description:
The local API of a running rnfs daemon (specification.md section 11; the route tables in `rnfs/api.py`). The CLI uses it for every command, and `rnfs.Client` is built on it; programs in other languages use it directly.

**Not stable yet.** No API stability is promised until rnfs 1.0.0: `rnfs.API_STATUS` is `provisional` (and `x-api-status` here), and routes, fields and statuses may change in 0.2.x releases. Ask `GET /api/capabilities` what a daemon offers. This document describes the API of the source tree it is in, whose `rnfs.__version__` is `info.version` (between releases that is the last release's, and what is marked "since 0.2.0" comes with the next); `tests/test_openapi.py` checks it against the code.

**Requests.**
- The API listens on the loopback only: 127.0.0.1 and, where the host has IPv6, ::1, on the same port (`api_port`, default 8788; a running daemon also writes it to `<rnfs dir>/daemon.json`). Clients must dial 127.0.0.1 itself. The `Host` header must be `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>` (403 `bad_host`), whichever address the request came to.
- Every route but `GET /api/status` and pairing's two (`POST` and `GET /api/apps/request`, which an app with no token yet uses) needs the token (security schemes `token` and `app`); without it: 403 `unauthorized`. The API never sends CORS headers.
- Before a client first sends the token, it should send `X-Rnfs-Challenge` on `GET /api/status` and check the `X-Rnfs-Proof` answered, so another program listening on the port while the daemon is down learns nothing (`rnfs.apiclient.api_proof`).
- GET parameters are in the query string; flags are true for `1`, `true` or `yes`. POST routes take a JSON object (at most 1 MiB; an empty body is `{}`), except the streamed uploads, whose bodies are the data. Bodies use Content-Length or chunked encoding. The API doesn't read Content-Type.
- Paths in parameters (`path`, `output`) are absolute paths on the daemon's machine.
- One request per connection (the connection is closed after it), but for a proof request kept open for one more.
- A known path asked with another method gets 405 `method_not_allowed` and `Allow`; an unknown path 404 `no_such_endpoint`.
- Every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

**Responses.** Successes are 200 with a JSON object, except the byte responses (`cat`, `name export`, `get/stream`, `export/stream`). Clients must ignore fields they don't know: fields are added in later versions.

**Errors** are `{"error": message, "code": code}` (`Error`, `ErrorCode`): the node's errors by status (ValueError 400 `bad_request`, NotFound 404 `not_found`, TooLarge 413 `too_large`, Denied 451 `denied`, InvalidDag 422 `invalid_dag`, Busy 503 `busy`, StorageFull 507 `storage_full`, anything else 500 `internal`), and the API's own refusals. Each operation lists the statuses it typically answers; any other is answered as `default` says. A 503 carries `Retry-After: 10`.

**Limits.** The request line, headers and a JSON body must arrive within 15 s (408 `timeout`); a streamed upload may pause up to 60 s between reads. At most 32 connections are served at once; more get 503 `too_many_connections` at once.

get.description: 404 `not_found` if the daemon doesn't have the feature.

Open: without a valid token it answers only `{"version"}` (a health check). With `X-Rnfs-Challenge` the response carries `X-Rnfs-Proof`; a client checks it before it first sends the token. Sent with `Connection: keep-alive` (and a valid challenge, and no body), the connection stays open for one more request, its last.

200.description: The full status with a valid token; else only the version.

anyOf.description: Without a valid token: only the version.

post.description: Answers, then stops the daemon as SIGTERM does and starts it again with the same command line, so settings that need a restart apply (on POSIX in place, keeping its process ID, so a service manager sees no exit; on Windows only under the task wrapper, which restarts it). The new run writes a new API token and has a new events epoch. 404 `unsupported` where it can't (daemon.json's `can_restart`). Since 0.2.1.

rnfs's and Reticulum's lines as the daemon's console shows them, the last 2000 kept in memory (nothing written; a restart starts afresh), so an app shows the log of a daemon it didn't start. Since 0.2.1.

post.summary: Ask for an app token (pairing; since 0.2.1)
post.description: No token: an app that has none asks for one. Show its code to the user, who approves the request where the CLI's token is (rnfs app requests, approve; an app such as RNFS Desktop, told by an `apps` event of change `requested`) after checking it shows the same code; then collect the token with GET /api/apps/request. Any valid name is answered alike, whether or not an app has it (a name taken is refused when the user approves), and a name may have several requests waiting, each with its own code. At most 32 requests wait at once, each for 10 minutes: a new one beyond takes the place of the oldest, whose app then finds it gone (404), as when it expires. The custom header keeps web pages from asking: their request would need a CORS preflight, which fails.

description.description: What the app says of itself, shown to the user.

secret.description: Only the requester has it: it collects the token with it.

code.description: Shown by the app and where the user approves, to tell this request from another under the same name.

expires.description: Unix time the request ends unanswered.

get.summary: What became of a pairing request (since 0.2.1)
get.description: No token: the requester's, with its secret. Once approved the token is given, a single time, and the request forgotten (404 after); a denied one is told once too.

parameters.name: X-Rnfs-Pairing-Secret
parameters.description: The secret POST /api/apps/request gave.

token.description: Present once approved: the app's token (X-Rnfs-Api, with X-Rnfs-App naming the app).

get.summary: The apps asking for a token (since 0.2.1)
get.description: The CLI's token only.

post.summary: Approve an app's request for a token (since 0.2.1)
post.description: The CLI's token only. Adds the app; its token is kept for the requester, who collects it (GET /api/apps/request): the approver never sees it. The other requests waiting under its name are denied. With `code`, approves only if it is the request's: 400 otherwise, the request still waiting. A name an app already has is refused here (400, a name clash), not when asked.

code.description: The code the app shows its user (optional: without it the request is approved unchecked). Approved only if it is the request's code, else 400. The CLI asks the user for it.

post.summary: Refuse an app's request for a token (since 0.2.1)
post.description: The CLI's token only.

token.name: X-Rnfs-Api
token.description: The CLI's token, which the daemon writes to `<rnfs dir>/api_token` (mode 0600) at each start; or, with `X-Rnfs-App`, that app's token (`rnfs app add`). Compared in constant time. Without `X-Rnfs-App` only the CLI's token passes, and with it only that app's. Every route but `GET /api/status` and pairing's `POST` and `GET /api/apps/request` needs it (403 `unauthorized`).

app.name: X-Rnfs-App
app.description: An app's name (since 0.2.0): the request is that app's, and `X-Rnfs-Api` carries its token. An app may do everything the CLI may but use the `/api/apps` routes (403 `forbidden`); that is no boundary, since it reads and writes files as the daemon's user (`add`, `get`, `export`) and so can reach the CLI's token: give an app a token only if you would trust it with the CLI. What it pins gets the source `app:<name>` (`app:<name>:<key>` with `X-Rnfs-Pin-Key`).

PinKey.name: X-Rnfs-Pin-Key
PinKey.description: An app's request only (since 0.2.0): pin and release as `app:<name>:<key>`, a group of the app's own pins. Refused (400) with the CLI's token, whose pins are always `user`'s, and when not a valid key.

Challenge.name: X-Rnfs-Challenge
Challenge.description: 32 lowercase hex digits. The response then carries `X-Rnfs-Proof`, which only a daemon knowing the token can make. Any request may carry it; clients send it on `GET /api/status` before they first send the token.

Proof.description: Answer to `X-Rnfs-Challenge`: hex(HMAC-SHA256(key, "rnfs api proof <port> <challenge>")), key being the token, or for a request with `X-Rnfs-App` that app's verifier (hex SHA-256 of "rnfs app token " + token). For an app the daemon doesn't have, it is keyed by a value no client knows (HMAC-SHA256 of a per-start secret and the name, since 0.2.0), so the response doesn't say whether the app exists; the client's check then fails.

BadRequest.description: A parameter or body the node refuses (`bad_request`).

Forbidden.description: Refused before routing: `bad_host`, or `unauthorized` (no valid token).

NotFound.description: `not_found`: no such content, path, name or alias, or no provider could supply it.

TooLarge.description: `too_large`, or `body_too_large` for a body over its limit.

LengthRequired.description: `length_required`: a body without Content-Length or chunked encoding.

Error.description: Any other error: `{"error", "code"}`, the status as `code` says (`internal` for 500).

warnings.description: What was skipped or changed, for the user (at most 100; see `warnings_total`).

warnings_total.description: How many warnings there were, present only past 100 (a tar upload).

name.description: A NomadNet snapshot: its entry name.

link.description: A NomadNet snapshot: the link, as normalised.

token.description: The app's token: given only this once.

count.description: How many changed (may exceed the CIDs listed).

path.description: The path from root to cid; [] for a bare CID.

pinned.description: The same content is pinned too.

capabilities.description: What this daemon offers beyond the routes themselves, each a promise kept once released.

routes.description: Every core and feature route, [method, path], by path.

overridden.description: Set on the command line, which wins.

nick.description: [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,31}, not 32 hex digits or a CID.

entries.description: The local list: CIDs and `sha256:<hex>` file hashes, sorted.

state.description: Free text: "" (not checked yet), in use, unresolved, fetching <cid>, or what failed.

Error.description: Every error the API sends (http.server's own error pages for a malformed request line aren't JSON).

ErrorCode.description: The machine-readable code of an error (rnfs.errors.CODES); never renamed once released. Clients must accept codes they don't know.

oneOf.description: 400: a parameter or body the node refuses (ValueError).
404: no such content, path, name, alias, pin or provider.
413: over a size or entry bound (max_download_size, max_output_entries, a quota, free space).
422: content whose DAG breaks the rules (specification section 5).
503: a local limit is reached; try again later (Retry-After: 10).
507: storing more would eat into the disk reserve.
500 (or any status without a code of its own): a bug or an unexpected failure; logged.
403: the Host header isn't 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port> (DNS rebinding).
403: no valid token (X-Rnfs-Api, with X-Rnfs-App for an app's).
404: no route has this path (an older daemon, or a feature not in it).
405: the path exists with another method; Allow lists those.
408: the request didn't arrive within request_timeout.
411: a body without Content-Length or chunked encoding.
413: a JSON body over 1 MiB, or a key over 64 KiB.
404: this daemon can't do that at all (no way to stop it, no event log).
503: max_connections are being served; sent before the request is read.
403: an app's token on a route only the CLI's token may use (/api/apps).
An upload's job was cancelled while it ran (409). Since 0.2.1.

Event.description: An event: `seq`, `kind`, `time` and the kind's own fields. Clients must ignore kinds and fields they don't know.

next.description: The `after` to ask with next (the last sequence given; 0 before any).

lost.description: Events the client asked for are gone (it fell behind, or the daemon restarted: `epoch` changed): every event held is given; reload your lists.

reason.description: Why it is paused; null otherwise.

root.description: The folder's root as last imported.

published.description: The root this sync last published.

next_publish.description: The earliest the next publish may be (Unix time), while within the hour since the last; null otherwise.

warning.description: POST /api/name/sync in private mode only: each publish's announce reaches outsiders.

state.description: Free text: waiting, current, unresolved, fetching <cid>, or what failed.

incomplete.description: Roots whose DAG the archive didn't complete.

size.description: Content bytes (a recipient's sealed file: the plaintext's).

sealed.description: Present (true) only for a sealed file.

recipient.description: A sealed file: whether this node is a recipient.

stored_size.description: A sealed file: the stored (encrypted) size.

name.description: A sealed file this node is a recipient of: its sealed name, null if not a safe file name.

sealed_folder.description: A sealed file this node is a recipient of: whether it is a sealed folder.

from.description: The node a get fetches from only.

error.description: Why it failed, as the equivalent call would say.

result.description: When done: what the equivalent call answers (a get's has `output` too).

runs.description: Times started (a restart runs it again).

rate.description: Bytes per second; null unless running.

path.description: add and import jobs: the path.

options.description: add jobs: the add options given.

source.description: The pin source, present when not `user` (an app's).

nomadnet.description: An add of a NomadNet link: the link.

retry_at.description: A get, pin or export queued again because its content wasn't found (rnfs 0.2.0): when it is tried again (Unix time); `error` says why. Null otherwise.

retry_since.description: Present while it waits to be tried again: when its content first wasn't found (Unix time). It is tried for up to 3 days from then.

retry.description: Present when it was submitted with `retry` true.

providers.description: While it runs (rnfs 0.2.0): the providers its fetch uses, not failed. Null before it has any, while not running, and for add and import jobs.

searching.description: While it runs (rnfs 0.2.0): true while its fetch searches the DHT for providers, which takes minutes on a radio before any byte arrives. False otherwise.

stream.description: An upload the API reads (POST /api/add/stream, /api/import/stream): listed and cancellable while it runs (the upload is answered 409 cancelled), never saved or resumed. Present only for those. Since 0.2.1.

stream_name.description: An upload's origin or name, if given. Present only for uploads.

Job.description: A background job (the jobs feature; specification section 11, Background jobs).

removed.description: Present on a job forgotten (`jobs clear`, or past `max_finished_jobs`), which carries only `id`, `job_kind`, `state` and this.

retry_at.description: When a job queued again because its content wasn't found is tried again (Unix time).

providers.description: The providers its fetch uses, while running (rnfs 0.2.0).

searching.description: Whether its fetch is searching for providers, while running (rnfs 0.2.0). A search beginning or ending is published at once.

JobEvent.description: A job changed state or progressed (the jobs feature).

exported.description: The key was exported (or imported). Since 0.2.0.

NameEvent.description: A newer record accepted for a name this node holds (its own, kept, followed, resolved) or a watched one.

warning.description: How to back the key up (a name can't move to another key).

last_heard.description: Unix time of its last announce or path response. A path response may come from any node with a path to it, so this is no sign the node is up: see last_seen.

rtt.description: The last link's round trip, seconds.

last_seen.description: Unix time of its last sign of life this run (an answer to a request, a request of its own served, a link established, or an announce of its own emitted recently); null if none. What online is decided from. Since 0.2.1.

PeerEvent.description: A peer appeared or went on- or offline (the peers feature).

type.description: null while the root block isn't stored.

sealed.description: Whether it is a sealed file; null when the stored blocks can't tell.

name.description: A local name: the label, else where it was added from, the shared-folder entry, or what a stored directory holds.

origin.description: Where it was added from on this machine. Since 0.2.0.

size.description: As its root block states it; null while not stored. Since 0.2.0.

entries.description: A directory's entry count; null for a file or while not known. Since 0.2.0.

added.description: When first pinned (Unix time); null for pins made before 0.2.0. Since 0.2.0.

Pin.description: A pin. The fields since 0.2.0 are always present from a 0.2.0 daemon.

source.description: The source that pinned or released; null for a label.

count.description: How many changed (may exceed the CIDs listed).

label.description: change label only: the new label, null when cleared.

warning.description: Private mode only: the name's announce reaches outsiders.

announce_held.description: Present while the node's clock is behind the name's last announce: why its announce is held (RNS drops an announce emitted no later than the one a node took its path from). The record is published (saved, pinned, kept); its announce goes out once the clock passes the last one, or after a week held in all (rnfs 0.2.0).

age.description: Seconds since the record was heard.

seen.description: When a check last found the node providing it (Unix time).

identity.description: side served: the identity that asked.

state.description: asked: waiting, done, missing, refused, released; served: waiting, fetching, pinned, dropped, refused, released.

retry_at.description: A pin waiting (reason `not_found`) whose content wasn't found yet: when it is tried again (Unix time; rnfs 0.2.0). Null otherwise.

file.description: The value in rnfs.toml, or null.

overridden.description: The daemon's command line sets it, and wins.

pending.description: rnfs.toml's value differs from the running one until a restart.

Setting.description: A setting: its schema entry, with its values.

size.description: null until the root block is stored.

blocks.description: Blocks known from the stored nodes (exact once every node is stored).

airtime.description: A slow node's radio measured its own airtime over budget.

upload_budget.description: The setting, bytes per hour (null or 0: none).

reticulum_interfaces.description: Reticulum's interfaces, read-only (attached to a shared instance, the instance's): what carries this node's traffic. rnfs doesn't change them: edit Reticulum's config, or rnsd's. Since 0.2.1.

full_name.description: As Reticulum writes it, e.g. TCPInterface[Hub/1.2.3.4:4242].

clients.description: Connected clients, for a server interface.

Status.description: GET /api/status with a valid token: the node's own fields and every loaded feature's (Feature.status). The schema is the union of its parts (`allOf`): a new field goes into the part that produces it (`StatusCore` for the node's own, `Status<Feature>` for a feature's; a new feature adds a part and lists it here). Clients must ignore fields they don't know.

identity_hash.description: The RNS identity hash, hex: the value other nodes list in `members` and `remote_pin_identities`.

nomadnet_identity_hash.description: The hash, hex, of the identity an add of a NomadNet link with `identify` identifies to the NomadNet node with (`storage/nomadnet_identity`, made at the first status if there is none, never the node's own): the value a NomadNet node's operator lists for pages it serves only to the identities it lists. Null if it can't be read or written. Since rnfs 0.2.0.

known_nodes.description: DHT servers in the routing table.

provided_entries.description: Entries inside pins provided that aren't provided as roots.

provide_entries_off.description: Why no entries are provided (the setting, or the airtime estimate); null when they are.

provide_entries_capped.description: Pins whose entries were left out at the cap.

max_storage.description: The max_storage setting: cached fetches are evicted while allocated_bytes is above it.

allocated_bytes.description: What the blocks stored take on disk: each block's size rounded up to allocation_unit, since each is a file of its own. What max_storage counts (rnfs 0.2.0).

allocation_unit.description: The bytes the blocks' filesystem allocates a file in (its block or cluster size, at least 4096), read at the start (rnfs 0.2.0).

unexported_names.description: Aliases of name keys never exported (or imported): losing one loses the name.

announces_held.description: Aliases of names whose announces are held: the clock is behind their last announce, which RNS would take them as replays of (rnfs 0.2.0).

clock_offset.description: How many seconds this node's clock seems behind the network's, estimated from the emission times of the announces it hears: the median over the nodes and names heard in the last 2 x announce_interval, one value each; null until 5 were. Never negative: a clock that looks ahead can't be told from announces delivered late, so it reads 0. Only reported, and logged past 5 minutes behind (rnfs 0.2.0).

local_servers.description: The DHT servers on this node's own island it knows of (spec section 6, "LoRa islands"); 0 on a node without a slow interface or local_interfaces.

partition.description: In partition mode: cut off from the servers beyond its island, lookups and publishes use local servers only.

partition_since.description: Unix time partition mode began; null when not in it.

StatusNetwork.description: What the node sees of the network, from its own state: nothing is sent to learn it (spec section 11, "Network status"). The routing table's servers (`known_nodes`), the local servers and partition mode are fields of `StatusCore`. The counts are kept in memory: a restart starts them afresh.

size_estimate.description: The number of DHT servers the density check estimates (spec section 6, "Network size estimate"); null until it pools enough complete lookups.

size_samples.description: Complete lookups (distinct keys) the estimate pools: up to 16, and it needs 8.

density_checked_hour.description: Searches and published keys the density check ran on in the last hour.

density_flagged_hour.description: Of those, the ones it fired on (servers packed near the key).

density_checked_day.description: Searches and published keys the density check ran on in the last day.

density_flagged_day.description: Of those, the ones it fired on. Without an attack a few percent fire.

blocks_refused_airtime.description: /blocks requests refused: a slow node's radio measured its own airtime over the last hour above its budget (spec section 3, "Measured airtime").

upload_budget_left.description: Bytes of `upload_budget` left; absent when no budget is set.

StatusRecordStore.description: The provider records this node stores for others against `record_budget`, and its storage tiers (spec section 6, "Provider records"); from counts kept in memory.

bytes.description: What counts against the budget: the state database's size in use (its other state included, such as block sizes), as last measured, and about 180 bytes for each record stored since.

capacity.description: Records the store would hold when full: those held plus the budget's room left at about 180 bytes a record, fewer while the free disk is short; those held once full.

full.description: Full: the storage tiers decide whose records are kept.

publishers.description: Publishers holding records here (this node included, if it does).

tiers.description: Each storage tier's fill and recent refusals and evictions.

StatusRecordTier.description: A storage tier: its records against its floor, and the new records refused and records evicted to make room (a full budget or a key's publisher cap) in the last hour and day, by the storer's tier and the evicted publisher's.

floor.description: The share of the budget a full store keeps for it.

refused_hour.description: New records of its publishers refused in the last hour.

refused_day.description: New records of its publishers refused in the last day.

evicted_hour.description: Records of its publishers evicted in the last hour.

evicted_day.description: Records of its publishers evicted in the last day.

unreferenced_blocks.description: Blocks nothing used before (an unpinned add's, say), collected with the records' own.

warnings.description: What was skipped or changed, for the user (at most 100; see `warnings_total`).

warnings_total.description: How many warnings there were, present only past 100.

sealed.description: Present (true) for a sealed file decrypted.

name.description: A sealed file: its sealed name, null unless a safe file name (a sealed folder: the directory's).

extracted.description: Present (true) when a sealed folder was unpacked.

ErrorLine.description: The last line of a streamed answer (application/x-ndjson) that failed after its first line: the error, its code and the status it would have had.

rtt.description: Seconds; null if the link couldn't be established.

reason.description: Why not, when rtt is null: no path within path_timeout; a path but not the node's identity; the identity known isn't the node's; not a member (private mode); the node closed the link as it was established (it is up, but refused); the link closed or wasn't established in time. Since 0.2.1.

hops.description: Hops of the path to the node once the ping ended; null without one. Since 0.2.1.

path_since.description: When Reticulum learned or last refreshed the path, Unix time. Since 0.2.1.

StatusSharedFolder.description: The shared folder (<rnfs dir>/files, or shared_folder) as its last scan left it, so an app needn't read the folder itself (it may not be able to: a Flatpak daemon, another user's). Since 0.2.1.

path.description: The folder, on the daemon's machine.

entries.description: Top-level entries imported and pinned (source folder).

bytes.description: Their content bytes, as their root blocks state them; null before the first scan ends.

last_scan.description: When the last scan ended, Unix time; null before the first.

refused.description: Why the folder isn't scanned (it leads into the rnfs dir); null if it is.

error.description: Why the last scan failed (the folder isn't a directory, a disk error); null if it didn't.

failed.description: Entries that couldn't be imported (their content refused, a full disk) or read whole.

failures.description: The first 10 of those, by name.

GcPreview.description: What gc would do now, nothing changed (dry_run; since 0.2.1), and what the stored blocks are kept for.

freed_bytes.description: Their bytes, as gc counts them.

allocated_bytes.description: What they take on disk (what max_storage counts).

held_back.description: A damaged DAG node something reaches: gc would delete nothing until `rnfs verify` removes it.

cached_fetches.description: The cached fetches gc would evict.

pinned_bytes.description: Stored block bytes a pin reaches.

cached_bytes.description: Those only a cached fetch reaches.

protected_bytes.description: Those only an operation in progress holds (a fetch, an add, a job).

records_bytes.description: What counts against record_budget: the state database, provider records stored for others and the rest of rnfs's state (record_store's bytes).

ConfigEvent.description: rnfs.toml was changed through the API (POST /api/config/set; not a dry run), from any client: what changed, what applied at once, what needs a restart, and every setting a restart would change now (GET /api/config's pending). Since 0.2.1.

applied.description: Applied to the running node now.

restart_required.description: Of those changed, whose new value applies at the next start.

pending.description: Every setting a restart would change, these changes or earlier ones (POST /api/restart applies them).

reason.description: Why it is paused; null otherwise.

root.description: The folder's root as last imported.

published.description: The root this sync last published.

next_publish.description: The earliest the next publish may be (Unix time), while within the hour since the last; null otherwise.

removed.description: The sync was stopped (POST /api/name/unsync, or its name removed).

NameSyncEvent.description: A name sync started, stopped, or changed state, reason or published root: its entry as GET /api/name/syncs lists it. Since 0.2.1.

AppsEvent.description: An app was given a token (rnfs app add, or a request approved) or removed, asked for one (pairing: show the user its id's request with its code), or was refused. Since 0.2.1.

code.description: change requested: the code the app shows.

StatusEvent.description: Top-level GET /api/status fields changed since the last check (every 30 s at most): fetch the status again. Since 0.2.1.

buckets.description: The buckets holding a node, by index.

index.description: i: its nodes are at distance [2^i, 2^(i+1)) from this node.

first_seen.description: Unix time (kept across a short absence).

last_heard.description: Unix time of its last announce or answer.

stale.description: Failed a query since last heard, or silent past two announce intervals: the first to give up its place.

dropped.description: Nodes that left whose seniority a return within two announce intervals regains.

unreliable.description: Nodes (in the table or not) whose last max_failures queries all failed, most recently failed first; at most 256.

retry_at.description: Unix time it may be queried again.

bans.description: Banned nodes, soonest to end first; at most 256.

reason.description: Why; null when not known (a ban from before a restart).

blackholed.description: Identities Reticulum blackholes: their nodes count as banned, without being listed in bans.

LogLines.description: The daemon's recent log lines (rnfs.recentlog). Since 0.2.1.

text.description: As the console shows it, non-printable characters escaped; at most 4096 characters.

next.description: Pass as after to get only newer lines.

dropped.description: Lines after after are no longer kept (it keeps the last 2000).
